correctness.rationale: The boundary phase derivative is a sum of Poisson kernels strictly decreasing on (0,π), giving exactly two cubic folds, with F''(0)=-U and F''(π)=V>0. The ± fold orientations and scales (2/(nU))^(1/3), (2/(nV))^(1/3) yield standard Airy integrals with correct signs; independent exact rational evaluation at a1=1/5,a2=1/2 verified U=207/16,V=1/3 and extreme velocities 9/2,1. The proof separates compact fold windows and uses cubic van der Corput n^-1/3, away-from-fold interior bound (n d)^-1/4 and outside 1/d to obtain normalized remainders O(M^(1-p/4)) and O(M^(1-p)), both vanishing exactly when p>4. Riemann sums supply both positive Airy masses; standard oscillatory Airy negative tail |s|^-1/4 is integrable to p-power for p>4. Independent finite-n Fourier coefficients trend correctly but do not prove the asymptotic limit. Assumptions exclude root collisions, noncollinear roots, p=4 and p=∞.

originality.rationale: The one-factor sharp order and coefficientwise Airy asymptotics are prior (Szehr–Zarouf 2017, Borichev–Fouchet–Zarouf 2021). The latter explicitly says on its PDF page 3 that exact cp moment constants are not studied and are left to forthcoming work; it concerns a single Blaschke factor. BFZ 2024 finite-product work treats sharp max-coefficient/l∞ decay in the accessible abstract, not this all-fixed finite-p two-fold moment formula. The paper's full body was inaccessible, and authorized institutional retrieval could not proceed because of a disconnected VPN. The present global tail argument is needed to upgrade local Airy profiles to exact summed p-moment constant. Higher-order stationary-phase general theory might implicitly cover the statement; originality remains best-of-knowledge.
